# 02 - NMC, NCA, NMCA, and High-Nickel Lithium-Ion Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

Primary sources:

- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2025, Electric vehicle batteries: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2025/electric-vehicle-batteries
- NHTSA, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles: Battery, Charging & Safety: https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/electric-and-hybrid-vehicles
- Argonne, scientists find new way to enhance durability of lithium batteries: https://www.anl.gov/article/scientists-find-new-way-to-enhance-durability-of-lithium-batteries
- Argonne, cathode design for lithium-ion batteries: https://www.anl.gov/article/argonne-builds-on-past-success-with-cathode-design-for-lithiumion-batteries

## What It Is

NMC means lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide. NCA means lithium nickel cobalt aluminum oxide. NMCA combines nickel, manganese, cobalt, and aluminum. These are layered lithium-ion cathodes typically designed for higher energy density than LFP.

## Automotive Relevance Today

These chemistries are central to longer-range and higher-performance EVs. IEA reports that NMC remains the most widely used chemistry in the United States and Europe, while LFP dominates more strongly in China.

High-nickel variants are especially relevant for:

- Long-range sedans and SUVs.
- Performance vehicles.
- Vehicles requiring high energy density in a fixed pack volume.
- Cold climates, where high-nickel chemistries often perform better than LFP.
- Towing or heavy vehicles where mass and packaging matter.

## Strengths

The central strength is energy density. NMC/NCA systems can store more energy per kg and per liter than LFP, enabling longer range, smaller packs, or better packaging.

They also support established global supply chains and years of field data across premium EV platforms. Argonne notes that NMC cathodes have been used in many electric cars and remain a focus for improving high-energy storage, charging, low-temperature performance, and safety.

## Weaknesses

The strategic weaknesses are cost, supply risk, and sustainability. Nickel and cobalt create exposure to price volatility, emissions, mining concentration, and ethical concerns. High-nickel cathodes can also become more reactive and difficult to stabilize as nickel content rises.

Operationally, many NMC vehicles recommend limiting routine charge to around 80% to preserve long-term battery health. This can reduce daily usable range compared with the headline pack size.

## Future Development

Development is moving toward:

- Less cobalt.
- Higher nickel with better coatings and gradients.
- Better cathode surface stability.
- More manganese-rich alternatives.
- Stronger electrolyte additives and thermal management.

Argonne research highlights dual-gradient and coating strategies to increase stability, lifetime, and energy density while reducing cost.

## Commercialization Outlook

NMC, NCA, and NMCA are mature and will remain important through the 2020s. They are unlikely to disappear quickly because premium and large vehicles still benefit from their energy density.

## Implications for Older EV Value

Older NMC/NCA cars may keep value if they deliver range, charging, and battery health that cheaper LFP cars cannot match. Their downside is that buyers may discount them if replacement costs are high, degradation is visible, or new LFP/LMFP cars offer sufficient range at much lower purchase prices.
